name: Electric Bikes
hub_intro: Ireland is quietly becoming an e-bike country: the Cycle to Work scheme covers e-bikes up to €1,500, fuel and parking costs keep climbing, and EU-legal pedelecs (250 W, assist to 25 km/h) need no licence, tax or insurance. We compare the e-bikes that suit Irish commutes, hills and weather — from €700 folders to €2,500 trekking machines.
guide: If you're a PAYE employee, the Cycle to Work scheme lets you buy an e-bike up to €1,500 through salary sacrifice — saving up to 52% depending on your tax band. Many bikes here fall under that ceiling deliberately.

Hub motors (in the wheel) are cheaper and fine for flat commutes. Mid-drives (at the pedals) use the bike's gears, climb far better and balance the bike — worth the premium in hilly Cork, Limerick or anywhere outside the city centre.
Battery: Wh is the number that matters

Ignore '50 km range' claims; look at watt-hours. 400 Wh is the practical minimum for daily commuting; 500+ Wh for 20 km+ round trips or hills. Real consumption is roughly 8–12 Wh per km in Irish conditions.
An e-bike without mudguards is a back-spray machine for eight months of the year here. Integrated lights running off the main battery mean you're never caught out by early winter darkness.

faqs.q: Do I need a licence or insurance for an e-bike in Ireland?
faqs.a: No — as long as it's a standard pedelec: 250 W motor, assistance cutting out at 25 km/h, and you have to pedal. More powerful e-bikes or throttle-driven ones are classed differently and need registration, insurance and a licence.

faqs.q: Can I get an e-bike on the Cycle to Work scheme?
faqs.a: Yes. The scheme covers pedelecs up to €1,500 (more than the €1,250 limit for regular bikes), via salary sacrifice through your employer. Higher-rate taxpayers effectively save around half the price. You can use it once every 4 years.

faqs.q: How far does an e-bike really go on one charge?
faqs.a: Divide battery watt-hours by 10 for a realistic Irish figure: a 400 Wh battery gives roughly 40 km of assisted riding with hills, wind and a stop-start commute. Eco mode stretches it; turbo mode halves it.

faqs.q: Are e-bikes OK in Irish rain?
faqs.a: Yes — motors and batteries on reputable brands are sealed for rain riding. Avoid pressure-washing, dry contacts before charging, and store the battery indoors in winter: cold storage below 5°C permanently eats capacity.

faqs.q: How much does charging an e-bike cost in Ireland?
faqs.a: A 500 Wh battery costs about 18–20 cents to charge fully at typical rates. Even commuting daily, that's under €50 a year — versus €1,500+ for a year of fuel or €1,000+ of public transport.

faqs.q: What's the difference between a €900 and a €2,000 e-bike?
faqs.a: Mostly the motor (mid-drive vs hub), battery brand (Bosch/Shimano cells vs generic), and components that survive year-round use: hydraulic brakes, better gears, integrated lights. If you ride daily, the upgrade pays for itself in reliability.

faqs.q: Can I ride an e-bike on Irish cycle lanes and greenways?
faqs.a: Yes — legal pedelecs are treated exactly like bicycles, so cycle lanes, greenways and bike parking are all available to you. The 25 km/h assist limit keeps them welcome on shared paths.

faqs.q: Should I buy a folding e-bike?
faqs.a: If your commute includes a train or you've nowhere secure to park, yes — a folder defeats both Irish bike theft and rail restrictions, since folded bikes travel free anytime on Irish Rail. Otherwise a full-size bike rides better.

pages.title: 5 Best Electric Bikes in Ireland 2026 — Tested & Compared
pages.desc: Ireland's best electric bikes for 2026, compared on motor, real range, hills and value — including Cycle to Work eligible picks under €1,500.
pages.h1: The 5 Best Electric Bikes in Ireland (2026)
pages.intro: The Irish e-bike market has matured fast: you can now get a genuinely good commuter for under €1,200 and a superb one under €2,000. We compared motors, honest range, braking, and weather-readiness across the most popular models sold here, flagging which qualify for the €1,500 Cycle to Work ceiling — because for most PAYE workers that scheme is an instant ~30–50% discount.

products.name: Decathlon Btwin LD 920 E
pros: Mid-drive torque at a hub-motor price
Hits the €1,500 Cycle to Work cap exactly
cons: 26 kg — heavy to lift onto racks
products.verdict: Nothing else under €1,500 combines a 70 Nm mid-drive, 540 Wh battery and full commuter kit. The default recommendation for any Irish commuter using Cycle to Work.

products.name: Engwe P20
pros: Torque sensor gives natural pedal feel
products.verdict: A maintenance-free city bike: belt drive plus torque sensor at €999 was unthinkable two years ago. Best for flat urban rides under 15 km.

products.name: Cube Touring Hybrid One 500
pros: Bosch motor + battery: the gold standard
Climbs anything in Ireland with ease
cons: Over the Cycle to Work cap
products.verdict: If the budget allows, this is the buy-once-cry-once choice: Bosch reliability, real 80 km range and a service network — an e-bike for the next decade.

products.name: Fiido D11
pros: Free on Irish Rail when folded
products.verdict: The mixed-commute special: fold it, hop the train, ride the last leg. Most battery per euro of any folding e-bike sold in Ireland.

products.name: Trek FX+ 2
pros: Rides like a normal bike — 18 kg
products.verdict: For riders who want fitness with a tailwind rather than a motorbike feel. The lightest, most natural-riding commuter here — just plan around the smaller battery.

pages.title: Best Electric Bikes Under €1,000 in Ireland (2026) — 5 Real Options
pages.desc: Five electric bikes under €1,000 actually worth buying in Ireland: honest range, decent brakes, real warranties. Compared for 2026.
pages.h1: Best Electric Bikes Under €1,000 in Ireland
pages.intro: Under €1,000, e-bike shopping is a minefield of no-name frames and warranty ghosts. But a handful of models deliver real quality at this price — and with Cycle to Work knocking up to 52% off, a €999 bike can cost a higher-rate taxpayer around €500 net. These five keep the essentials: branded cells, disc brakes, and someone to call when things go wrong.

products.name: Engwe P20
pros: Belt drive: no oil, no rust, no maintenance
products.verdict: The most refined ride under €1,000, full stop. City dwellers with flat commutes get a premium experience at half the usual cost of one.

products.name: Eleglide M1 Plus
pros: 21 gears + suspension handle hills and trails
cons: Needs setup care out of the box
products.verdict: Kilometres per euro champion. The assist is less polished than pricier rivals, but a 450 Wh battery and full gearing at €749 forgives a lot.

products.name: Fiido D11
pros: Genuine 40 km+ range in a folder
products.verdict: If storage or train legs are part of your life, this is the sub-€1,000 answer. Range and weight figures embarrass folders at twice the price.

products.name: Decathlon Btwin E-Fold 500
products.verdict: Buy this for the safety net: walk-in service and a lifetime frame warranty remove every risk that makes people fear cheap e-bikes.

products.name: ADO Air 20
pros: 16 kg, belt drive AND hydraulic brakes
products.verdict: The folding twin of the Engwe P20's philosophy: belt drive, torque sensor, hydraulics — specs from the €2,000 class squeezed under €1,000.

pages.title: Best Folding Electric Bikes Ireland 2026 — Top 5 for Train & Apartment Life
pages.desc: The 5 best folding e-bikes in Ireland for commuters using Irish Rail, DART or short on storage. Weight, fold size and range compared.
pages.h1: Best Folding Electric Bikes in Ireland
pages.intro: Folding e-bikes solve the three most Irish bike problems at once: theft (it lives indoors), rain (take the train when it lashes, folded bikes travel free on Irish Rail), and apartment storage. The compromise is small wheels and weight — so we ranked these five on fold speed, carry weight, and how much riding quality survives the hinge.

products.name: ADO Air 20
pros: Belt + torque sensor + hydraulics in a folder
16 kg is carryable for most adults
cons: 345 Wh suits sub-15 km commutes best
Folded size still bulky for car boots
products.verdict: The best-riding folder under €1,500: it loses almost nothing to full-size bikes on smooth tarmac and gains a maintenance-free drivetrain.

products.name: Brompton Electric C Line
pros: Folds to airline-cabin size — nothing comes close
Battery detaches as a carry bag
products.verdict: The only e-bike that disappears under a desk or luggage rack. If your commute is truly multimodal — bus, train, office — the fold justifies the fortune.

products.name: Fiido X
pros: Real 50 km+ range, exceptional for a folder
products.verdict: For longer commutes that still need a fold at each end. Twice the practical range of a Brompton at a third of the price — if you can lift it.

products.name: Decathlon Btwin E-Fold 900
products.verdict: The pragmatist's folder: full gears, hydraulics, big battery and a shop in every city that fixes it while you wait.

products.name: Engwe C20 Pro
cons: 24 kg defeats the point of folding for many
products.verdict: A folding bike for storage rather than carrying: if the fold is for the hallway, not the train, its huge battery and price are unbeatable.

pages.title: Best Electric Mountain Bikes Ireland 2026 — Top 5 eMTBs Compared
pages.desc: Ireland's best electric mountain bikes for trail centres like Ticknock and Ballyhoura — motors, suspension and batteries compared for 2026.
pages.h1: Best Electric Mountain Bikes in Ireland
pages.intro: From Ticknock to Ballyhoura to the Wicklow gap roads, Ireland's trail scene rewards an eMTB's superpower: doing three climbs in the time one used to take. eMTB prices have finally relaxed, with credible hardtails under €2,000. We compared motor torque, battery size, suspension quality and the component compromises each brand chose.

products.name: Decathlon Rockrider E-EXPL 520
cons: Hardtail only — rough on technical descents
products.verdict: The eMTB that opened the sport to normal budgets. For Irish trail-centre riding (mostly groomed climbs and flow descents), the hardtail compromise barely matters.

products.name: Cube Reaction Hybrid Performance 625
products.verdict: The benchmark hardtail eMTB: Bosch's mid-range motor with a big battery means full Ballyhoura days without range anxiety.

products.name: Giant Talon E+ 3
pros: Giant dealers in every Irish county
cons: 50 Nm is the weakest motor here
products.verdict: The safe buy: not the strongest motor, but flawless support coverage and the most natural-feeling assist for newcomers to off-road riding.

products.name: Engwe Engine Pro 2.0
pros: Fat tyres float over mud and gravel
Full suspension at a hardtail price
cons: More trekking toy than true MTB
products.verdict: Not a trail weapon — a go-anywhere adventure tank for towpaths, beaches and forest roads. Judged as that, it's tremendous fun per euro.

products.name: Specialized Turbo Tero 3.0
pros: Top-tier app with tuning and anti-theft
cons: 50 Nm needs lower gears on steep climbs
products.verdict: One bike for everything: weekday commuter (add mudguards), weekend trail bike (remove them). The most versatile eMTB sold in Ireland.

pages.title: Best Commuter Electric Bikes Ireland 2026 — Top 5 for Daily Riding
pages.desc: The best commuter e-bikes in Ireland for daily, year-round riding: integrated lights, mudguards, racks and real range. 2026 comparison.
pages.h1: Best Commuter Electric Bikes in Ireland
pages.intro: A proper commuter e-bike earns its keep every single weekday: integrated lights you never charge, mudguards that keep work clothes dry, a rack for the laptop bag, and a lock-friendly frame. We compared five commute-ready machines on the boring details that decide whether you're still riding in February — not just the spec-sheet heroes.

products.name: Decathlon Btwin LD 920 E
products.verdict: The complete commuter under the scheme cap. Tally the cost of adding lights, rack, and mudguards to rivals and the value gap only widens.

products.name: Cube Touring Hybrid One 500
products.verdict: The ten-year commuter. Bosch's motor and battery ecosystem plus Cube's build make this the bike to retire your car payment for.

products.name: Gazelle Paris C7 HMB
products.verdict: Commuting in normal clothes at a conversational pace — the Dutch formula executed perfectly. For comfort-first riders nothing here comes close.

products.name: Eleglide T1 Step-Thru
products.verdict: The budget bike that copies the right homework: commuter essentials all present at a price where rivals delete them. Setup care required, then it just works.

products.name: Tenways CGO600 Pro
pros: 16 kg — carry it up steps easily
products.verdict: The anti-tank: half the weight of traditional commuters with a sealed, greaseless drivetrain. City riders with stairs in their life, start here.
